about:
Manufacture Nevada operates from Reno, Nevada As the official representative of the MEP National Network in the state, it functions as a publicly funded manufacturing extension partnership. The center receives funding from grants and public partners to subsidize consulting and training services for Nevada manufacturers.

The organization provides three core service lines: Business Growth consulting to help manufacturers navigate challenges and identify opportunities; Workforce Solutions including leadership workshops, cross-training programs, and manager skills development; and Manufacturing Operations consulting focused on process improvement, productivity, and profitability. It also delivers specialized training such as Lean Six Sigma Black Belt, PCQI 2.0 for food safety, and leadership workshops across Northern and Southern Nevada.

Manufacture Nevada serves manufacturers across Nevada, connecting them with resources, partners, and funding. Documented client engagements include EIS Automation, which secured $2 million in growth capital; Pilula; K2 Energy Solutions; and Alpha Productions Technologies. The center's network spans businesses, organizations, and resources throughout Nevada and the U.S.

The center's funding model distinguishes it from private consultants: public funding allows more affordable access to expert advisors, and its success is measured solely by client outcomes. As an MEP National Network representative, it provides access to opportunities available only through publicly funded programs.

name: Manufacturing Technologies, Inc. (MTI)
about:
Manufacturing Technologies, Inc. (MTI) operates from a 23,000-square-foot facility in Bernalillo, New Mexico, just north of Albuquerque. The company traces its roots to 1989, when it began as a small manual machine shop in Albuquerque. Over the decades it has evolved into a contract precision manufacturer offering both CNC machining and fabrication under one roof. The business is led by President Lucas Bulow.

MTI provides CNC machining and precision fabrication services in-house. Its machining capabilities include 5-axis milling, 3-axis turning, and wire EDM, with the ability to hold tolerances tighter than 0.0005 inch. The fabrication side covers CNC laser cutting, press brake forming, and MIG and TIG welding; the laser system can maintain ±0.005 inch on profiles from 0.001 to 0.375 inch thick. The company works with a wide range of metals — including hardened steel, stainless, titanium, tungsten, rhenium, nickel-based alloys, copper, brass, tantalum, and aluminum — as well as plastics. Operations run out of a 23,000-plus-square-foot plant.

The shop serves aerospace, defense, fluid-handling, oil-and-gas, and transportation sectors, supplying both private-sector and government customers. Its AS9100D/ISO 9001:2015 certification and ITAR registration enable it to handle defense and aerospace work that requires controlled documentation and export compliance.

MTI emphasizes its willingness to tackle complex, challenging parts while maintaining quality and on-time delivery. The company describes its model as selling flexibility — accepting any material, quantity, or complexity — and backs that with lean manufacturing techniques, advanced software, and high-end tooling to keep pricing competitive.

about:
Maple Lane Variety Fab operates a full-service welding and fabrication shop in Kawkawlin, Michigan, serving the greater Bay City and Tri-Cities region. The company provides custom metal fabrication, welding, and inspection services for both residential and commercial customers.

The shop runs a range of value-added processes under one roof, including MIG, TIG, and stick welding on mild steel, aluminum, stainless steel, cast iron, and specialty alloys; CNC plasma cutting; press-brake forming; tube bending; sand and media blasting; and painting. It also maintains an inspection department staffed by American Welding Society Certified Welding Inspectors who perform dry magnetic particle, dye penetrant, structural steel, RCSC bolting, pan decking, shear stud, and dry film thickness examinations, and who can qualify welders and procedures to AWS D1.1.

Customers span agricultural, industrial, and structural steel sectors, with typical work covering ornamental and safety railings, metal signage, indoor and outdoor furniture, structural frameworks, and repair of farm and heavy equipment. The company offers mobile welding and repair crews that travel throughout the Tri-Cities area.

Maple Lane Variety Fab positions itself as a one-stop metal fabrication source, eliminating the need to coordinate multiple vendors for cutting, forming, welding, inspection, and finishing. Its AWS-certified inspection capability and ability to qualify welding to code are cited as key differentiators.

about:
Marchant Schmidt Inc. operates from Fond du Lac, Wisconsin, where it has manufactured industrial food cutting solutions for more than 60 years. The company emphasizes family values as a driver of innovation and customer partnerships, and serves global markets from manufacturing sites in both the United States and the United Kingdom.

The company designs and builds cheese converting equipment, specialty food cutting machines, hygienic automation systems, and inspection systems. Its engineering team provides custom engineered solutions, using multiple generations of conceptual drawings to optimize product flow and line layout. Capabilities extend to presale consultation, installation, operator training, and ongoing service supported by technicians, programmers, mechanical and electrical engineers, and robotic specialists.

Marchant Schmidt serves food processing sectors including cheese, bakery, confectionery, and canning. Recent applications include precise powder application on shredded cheese, shredding and grating non-dairy cheese, high-speed loaf cake cutting, and hygienic robotic food loading. The company also supplies replacement parts and rebuilding services for continuous cooker valves, hydrostatic cookers, Graco lubricators, and scale feed conveyors.

The company states that its family values underpin a commitment to look beyond individual machines to optimize entire production lines, and points to an extensive list of lifetime customer partnerships as evidence of its dedication to stand behind what it builds.

about:
Marian's Medical Supplies, LLC opened in 2008 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. The limited-liability company was formed to supply durable medical equipment and diabetic products to adults and children throughout Baton Rouge and the surrounding parishes.

The firm operates as a distributor, stocking a broad catalog from multiple brands across categories that include mobility aids, respiration equipment, hospital beds, wound-care products, incontinence supplies, orthopedic devices, and personal protective equipment. Staff work with each client or patient to customize fittings and configurations, and orders ship from the Baton Rouge warehouse.

Primary customers are home-healthcare patients, caregivers, and clinical practices in the Greater Baton Rouge area that need durable medical equipment, diabetic supplies, and related consumables. The company also serves business clients such as nursing facilities and ambulance services that require ambulance equipment, bathroom-safety gear, and rehabilitation devices.

The company's stated motto, "Customer Friendly-Prompt Delivery," reflects its emphasis on responsive service, reliability, and dedication. Leadership says it continuously expands its product lines to ensure immediate availability for both patients and business accounts.

name: Marine Electric Systems LLC
old_description: No shortcuts. No guesswork. Just reliable power systems built to perform when it matters most.
about:
Marine Electric Systems LLC operates from Annapolis, Maryland, where it serves as a marine electrical and electronics specialist. The company marked its presence with a grand opening at Bert Jabin's Yacht Yard in Annapolis on October 12, though its founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The firm provides installation and integration services for a range of marine power systems, including lithium battery banks with intelligent battery management, inverter/chargers that deliver clean AC power, high-output alternators, solar arrays, shore power connections, windlass and thruster units, electronic navigation suites, and high-efficiency air conditioning. It also stocks and sells Ancor-branded electrical components such as tinned copper lug kits and UV-resistant cable ties.

Its customers are primarily recreational and commercial vessel owners—yachts, sailboats, and powerboats—that require reliable electrical and electronic systems for offshore and coastal operation. The company's work spans new installations, upgrades, and system retrofits for both private owners and marine service yards.

Marine Electric Systems emphasizes a "no shortcuts, no guesswork" approach, aiming to deliver power systems that perform dependably when it matters most. The company positions itself as an expert resource for marine electrical design, installation, and ongoing support.

about:
Mark Electronics Inc was incorporated in 1992 in Glenside, Pennsylvania. The company operates as a Defense Logistics Agency designated Small-Business Set Aside (SBSA) distributor, focusing on military distribution services for original equipment manufacturers and other manufacturers.

The firm provides procurement, contract administration, and military packaging services, including pre-award and post-award contract administration for military procurement contracts. It manages DLA procurement contracts for the small-business set-aside aftermarket on behalf of Ducommun and distributes electronic components for partners such as Seal Dynamics, Graywacke, and SCI. Services span acquisition, inspection, packaging, distribution, and resale of electronic components.

Mark Electronics serves the defense, aviation, space, and military sectors, working directly with the Defense Logistics Agency and OEMs. Its customer base includes manufacturers requiring military spare-part aftermarket support, with concrete relationships including Ducommun, Seal Dynamics, Graywacke, and SCI.

The company states that its goal is to provide supply chain solutions to manufacturer and OEM partners, emphasizing expertise in all aspects of doing business with the DLA. It was founded to address the challenging and costly operation of supporting military spare-part aftermarket procurement requirements.

name: Mark Lackley Furniture Maker
old_description: One-of-a-kind, custom handcrafted poker and game tables, meticulously made in Vermont.
about:
Mark Lackley Furniture Maker operates from a woodshop in Taftsville, Vermont. The business traces its start to 2006, when founder Mark Lackley built a custom poker table for a hedge-fund manager from Armonk, New York, complete with drink holders fashioned from refurbished brass artillery shells. Lackley, an Atlanta native and Yale graduate who has lived in Vermont since 2001, runs the company with his wife and business partner, Kim. The venture gained momentum after Maine furniture maker Thomas Moser praised the piece at a fine-furnishings show, urging Lackley to produce more.

The shop produces one-of-a-kind, handcrafted poker and game tables. Each piece is built to order, incorporating custom designs such as reversible tabletops that convert between poker and dining or conference use, varied base styles, integrated chip wells, drink holders, and tailored armrests. Work combines traditional woodworking — joinery, veneering, and intricate inlay — with light fabrication, including custom-welded stainless-steel and brass components for hardware and lighting. No facility dimensions or headcount are disclosed; output is measured in individual commissions rather than batch volumes.

Clients span high-net-worth individuals, corporate executives, and entertainment-industry figures. Notable commissions include a table for Guy Laliberté, co-founder of Cirque du Soleil, and a reversible conference/poker table for an executive office. The tables have also been featured in Architectural Digest, the Robb Report, and the New York Times, with most new business arriving through word of mouth.

The founder's 30 years at the bench, spanning cabinetmaking, welding, and bookbinding, underpin the blend of artistry and engineering that defines each table.

name: Mark Richey Woodworking and Design
old_description: The highest quality architectural woodwork and corporate furniture expertly built for exceptional clients
about:
Mark Richey Woodworking and Design operates from a 105,000-square-foot facility in Newburyport, Massachusetts. The company was founded in 1981 by Mark and Teresa Richey and is certified as a woman- and minority-owned business. Over four decades it has grown into a national provider of architectural woodwork and corporate furniture, with a division called WallGoldfinger Furniture dedicated to custom workplace furnishings.

The shop combines high-tech tooling — CNC routers, state-of-the-art finishing lines — with traditional hand craftsmanship to produce acoustic panels, curved wood elements, custom trim, staircases, museum displays, window walls, and full wall-paneling systems. On the furniture side it builds boardroom tables, conference and dining pieces, desks, credenzas, lecterns, moot-court furniture, banquettes, and collaborative seating, including the proprietary Doko product line.

Clients span academic, corporate, museum, performing-arts, residential, restaurant, retail, and hospitality sectors. Notable installations include the LEGO Group’s U.S. headquarters in Boston, the CarGurus office, Novartis Biomedical Research’s U.S. headquarters, the Met’s 81st Street Studio, and a Midwest contemporary residence designed by Peter Rose Architects.

The founders frame the business around sustainability — the plant runs on clean-burning biomass heat — and inclusivity, aiming to mentor a new generation of craftspeople from historically marginalized groups. Leadership emphasizes fused art-and-technology craftsmanship, integrated project teams, and a promise to meet deadlines without sacrificing quality.

old_description: You will find value and opportunitieswith Marlex whether you are a pharmacy buyer looking to improve your bottom line or a manufacturer seeking new distribution.
about:
Marlex Pharmaceuticals Inc, based in New Castle, Delaware, positions itself as a generics-focused enterprise serving pharmacy buyers and manufacturers seeking distribution channels. The company runs a manufacturing facility designed for production innovation and inflexible quality standards, with packaging lines capable of bottling 200,000 to 400,000 assorted bottles per month. Its capabilities span pharmaceutical and drug distribution, packaging, labeling, heat induction foil sealing, and manufacturing. Quality assurance operates under cGMP regulations, encompassing batch record review, product release, and inspection of incoming components from contract manufacturers and repackagers.

Marlex serves the pharmaceutical, health care, hospital, and retail sectors. Its customer base includes pharmacy buyers aiming to improve their bottom line, pharmaceutical manufacturers seeking new distribution channels, and health care providers requiring reliable drug supply and related services.

The company’s stated mission is to deliver great products and services that drive quality and efficiency in pharmaceutical care to improve patients’ lives. It differentiates itself through a focus on supply chain efficiencies, operational excellence, and patient safety, with the goal of becoming the preferred partner for both pharmaceutical manufacturers and health care providers.
